stem:
Meena's teacher writes 'air' on the blackboard and asks the class how it should be classified. Meena knows that air contains nitrogen, oxygen, argon, carbon dioxide and water vapour, and that these gases are mixed together without chemically combining with one another.

How should air be classified?

options.text: A compound, because it contains more than one kind of substance
An element, because the gases in it keep their own properties
A mixture, because several gases are present together without being chemically combined
A pure substance, because it looks uniform and has no visible parts

teacher.key_rationale: Air contains nitrogen, oxygen, argon, carbon dioxide and water vapour mixed together without chemical bonding, so it is a mixture: option C. Option A traps students who think 'several substances present' automatically means compound; D traps students who classify by uniform appearance; B misuses the idea of retained properties.
